主要内容: Most of the revenue for the top five U.S. insurers comes from Medicare and Medicaid, according to a report published in Health Affairs. The combined revenue from these government-sponsored health programs grew from $92.5 billion in 2010 to $213.1 billion in 2016, representing nearly 60% of their total revenue. This growth coincided with the implementation of the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare), which required nearly all Americans to have health coverage. The report highlights that while the largest insurers have reduced their presence on Obamacare exchanges, they continue to profit from government-run programs. The authors suggest that requiring insurers to participate in Obamacare marketplaces could improve access to health coverage. Medicaid and Medicare enrollment in the top five insurers increased from 12.8 million to 25.5 million between 2010 and 2016. The report also notes that these insurers remained profitable during this period.
